question.problem: The average temperature in the Arctic in December of a particular year was ${3.2}^{∘}\,\text{C}.$ Due to plummeting temperatures in the winter, the average temperature in February of the next year decreased by ${6.9}^{∘}\,\text{C}$ compared to the average temperature in December. What was the average temperature in the Arctic in February?
question.worked_solution:
To determine the average temperature of the Arctic in February, we subtract the change in temperature (from December to February) from the average temperature in December. This gives

$$
{3.2}^{∘}\,\text{C}-{6.9}^{∘}\,\text{C}=-{3.7}^{∘}\,\text{C}.
$$

Consequently, the average temperature in the Arctic at the end of February was $-{3.7}^{∘}\,\text{C}.$
